narrative.overview:
Healthcare Uncharted looks like a working explorer's atlas of the healthcare system: dense with real data, annotated in monospace, built to be used in the field rather than admired on a shelf. Every surface starts from deep navy water, and the content IS the light: white display type, fog-blue prose, and one teal signal that marks where the reader should look next. Data is never decoration here. Numbers arrive with their sources, maps carry real coordinates, and the interface treats the reader like the person at the chart table, not a passenger.

The system is tactile and confident. Cards lift when you reach for them, buttons press, and arrows slide toward where you are going, all inside a strict motion budget (150ms state changes, 280ms structural moves, 250ms ceiling on phones, stillness under reduced motion). Density is medium-high and unapologetic: this is an atlas, and atlases are full. What keeps the fullness readable is discipline, one-pixel sounding lines around every container, a four-step tonal ladder instead of shadow soup, and monospace labels that caption everything like coordinates on a chart.

The Brass Instruments era (adopted 2026-10-11, DECISIONS BR1 to BR3, after four rounds of mockups in docs/HU-DESIGN-DIRECTION-2026-10-11.md). The site is a set of instruments. Things you press are keys, raised on a floor with a fine brass edge, and they sink when pressed. Brass marks three things only: the one main act on a screen, the place you are or the choice that is on, and the frame of a featured panel. Panels are faces, readouts are recessed glass that stays dark in both themes the way a device's screen does in daylight, fields are recessed wells (glass at night, light in day, on David's review), and nothing glows. Night is the navy the site always had; day is white panels on a cool slate ground with tight shadows and the same brass. The working guide is docs/HU-BRASS-LOOK-2026-10-11.md and the recipes live in the last section of hu-global.css. The design phase CLOSED 2026-10-12 (DECISIONS BR4) after David's page-by-page review of every page in both themes; Tier 3 below is what shipped, and the change budget governs it again.

It replaced the Quiet Precision era (2026-08-06 to 2026-10-11, from the Reskin Lab: Signal Boost, then Quiet Precision, then Cartographic Quiet), described here for the record: Hierarchy comes from type and space, not from effects. State is ink and weight, never a halo. Boxes dissolve into rules: stat tiles stand on a 2px top rule instead of sitting in a filled box, callouts read as margin notes on open ground, toolbars are mastheads over one strong rule. The cartographic layer whispers on top: hairline survey ticks at two corners of outer surfaces, drawn in border gray and never in accent; names at drawer-card scale in tracked caps; fact labels as mono captions; tiny geometric markers leading catalog rows. The stated anti-goal, in the founder's words: nothing that feels AI generated fast and dirty. Glows, gradient accent bars, tinted callout panels, and 300-weight body on dark are all retired.
keyCharacteristics: Dark-first: deep navy pages where content carries the light; a full light theme exists and flips by token, never by redesign
Brass (#D9B56A) does the acting and marks where you are; one teal signal (#4ECDC4) still points: focus rings, live values
State is brass: the choice that is on is a brass key with brass ink, never a glow
Monospace is the voice of data: every label, source line, and coordinate is IBM Plex Mono, small and letterspaced
Depth is physical: keys on a floor, framed faces, recessed glass; shadows fall downward and never radiate
Real data density, phone-honest: 44px touch floor and a one-transient-surface rule on every interactive tool

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Signal Teal points: the focus ring, the live value, the place to look. If teal is everywhere, it is nowhere. Since 2026-10-11 brass owns the main act and the choice that is on, so teal can stay a signal.

rules.name: The Deep-Step Rule
rules.body: Any accent used as TEXT on a light surface drops to its deep step (`--teal-dk`, `--amber-dk`, or the per-lens dark values). Tinted backgrounds keep the bright hue; text never does.

rules.name: The Earned Color Rule
rules.body: Data color appears only when the reader chose the metric. Maps rest in neutral teal-tinted fills until a lens or shading is picked; a tint nobody asked for reads as unexplained decoration.

rules.name: The Brass State Rule (was the Ink State Rule, rewritten 2026-10-11)
rules.body: State is a material, never light. Active means a brass key with brass ink (#2A1D08) and weight 700: the current tab, view, filter, switch, the section in the top bar. It never means a glow, a halo or a tinted wash. Inside a data drawing a selection may still use ink and weight, the way print does.

rules.name: The Data Speaks Mono Rule
rules.body: If a string is a value, a unit, a source, a date, or a coordinate, it is set in IBM Plex Mono. If it is a sentence, it is DM Sans. No exceptions; this is how readers learn what is checkable.

rules.name: The CAPS Rule
rules.body: Emphasis is CAPS or a heavier weight, never italics and never bold-inside-prose. UI strings follow the same voice kernel as editorial: no em dashes, middots (·) join fragments.

rules.name: The Legibility Floor Rule (adopted 2026-08-09, given two values 2026-09-20)
rules.body: Functional text, anything a reader must read to use the page (labels, tags, kickers, meta, source lines, nav items), never sets below `--t-label`: 13px on a phone, 11px on a desktop. Nothing sets below `--t-micro` on either. Tracked-caps mono labels are NOT exempt; a third of the audience is on phones, and decorative smallness was the old habit.

rules.name: The Caption Rule
rules.body: Fact-row labels and data captions are mono captions: 11px, uppercase, tracked 0.12em or wider, FOG BLUE (`--t2`). Faded Ink captions failed David's QA on open dark ground once the tile boxes dissolved (2026-08-06); Faded Ink is reserved for source lines, meta, and section labels that should recede. Names at drawer-card scale go tracked caps (14px / 0.09em); page H1s and editorial card titles stay mixed-case Outfit 800. Values keep `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` wherever figures align vertically.

rules.name: The Border-First Rule
rules.body: If a container needs definition at rest, it gets a Sounding Line border and a tonal step, never a shadow. A shadow at rest must be justified by floating above a live canvas.

rules.name: The Survey Tick Rule
rules.body: Outer surfaces (content cards, pin cards, drawer panels, report containers) may carry two hairline corner ticks: 10px arms, 1px, Sounding Line Bold, top-left and bottom-right, inset about 5px. Ticks are drawn in border gray, NEVER in an accent hue, and never on nested elements; the frame is marked the way a chart plate is, quietly and at the edge.

rules.name: The Hub Lift Rule (V3 hub surfaces, locked 2026-08-06)
rules.body: The hub pages (home, tools, learn indexes) are PRODUCT surfaces, not documents: their catalog cards and the search box carry RESTING elevation as an interaction affordance. Vocabulary: search box `0 12px 32px rgba(0,0,0,.55)`, catalog cards `0 10px 28px rgba(0,0,0,.45)` on the Raised-Chart-plus (#131f30 family) step. This is a scoped exception to the Border-First Rule, which continues to govern reading and editorial surfaces unchanged. Source: the V3 Field Office comp (docs/HU-V3-HOME-BUILD-SPEC-2026-08-06.md).

rules.name: The Earned Scenery Rule (V3, 2026-08-06; RETIRED 2026-10-11, HX2)
rules.body: The home hero's canvas world used to draw only after a tap on the compass. Now the honeycomb is there from the start and the seven Atlas zones stand on it as raised tiles routed to the compass, each a link into the Atlas; the map moves for 20 seconds, slows, rests at 30, and wakes on a hover or a press. Reduced motion draws it still.

dos: Do keep the 44px touch floor, the 699px phone line measured on the shorter side (`max-width:699px, max-height:500px`, both halves), and the 250ms phone motion cap on every interactive surface.
Do hold the phone type floor: functional text never below `--t-label` (13px), nothing below `--t-micro` (12px). Set sizes from the tokens, never from a literal. See "The Two Surfaces".
Do give a phone ONE top bar: the site nav or a page toolbar, never both, plus at most one bottom bar, inside 20 percent of the viewport. The browser takes another quarter we do not control.
Do flip accent text to its deep step on light surfaces (The Deep-Step Rule).
Do check every reskinned surface in BOTH themes; a rule that vanishes on light is a regression, not a style.
Do build controls from the recipes in hu-global.css (keys, brass, faces, glass): use the class, or give a page's own selector the recipe properties; never copy a gradient (since 2026-10-11).
Do press with keys: navy at night, white in day, a fine brass top edge, a floor under it, sinking on press. The logo is a key.
Do keep brass scarce: the one main act on a screen, the choice that is on, the section you are in, the frame of a featured panel. Body text is never brass.

Do put readouts (stat tiles, clocks, scores, the year pill) on recessed glass that stays dark in both themes, with the glass inks. A page's own header band of numbers takes the field tokens and goes light in day (the Data Observatory band and the Traffic tiles, his review).
Do put everything you type into or pick in on the field tokens: glass at night, white in day (search, inputs, editors, save boxes, segment tracks).

Do give day its own ground: cool slate #E1E7EF (#EDF1F6 at the top of a page) under white panels with #F9FBFD feet, #B4C0CF edges, and shadows 2 to 10px tight under the thing. Never a wide soft shadow on a light ground.
Do let panels be faces with a downward depth shadow; a catalog card is a face in a brass frame.

Do draw the compass rose in its brass dial on home, the light rose in day, its lines heavier when it is drawn big; on a desk the honeycomb carries the seven Atlas zones as raised tiles routed to it, and the map rests after 30 seconds.

Do keep reading pages quiet at the end: no Share button on a Learn module or a Rounds piece (a reader copies the address), the sources list folded shut ("Show all N sources"), then the keep-reading card.
Do keep home and the footer short: on a desk, three picks under the hero and an All tools key; a footer without a signup, and on a phone only the support key, the copyright and the policy links.
Do caption every data element in Plex Mono with its source; a number without a walkable source does not ship.
donts: Don't let a canvas scale its UI text with its geometry. Terrain may scale on a pinch-zoom surface; the panels, tabs and status lines that report state never do.
Don't stack transient surfaces; one sheet, drawer, or overlay at a time on phones.
Don't set body or description text at weight 300 on dark; 400 is the floor.
Don't color data the reader did not ask for; resting maps stay neutral (The Earned Color Rule).
Don't glow, anywhere: no colored blur in a shadow, no text-shadow halo, no radiance on hover or focus (The Brass State Rule). There is no exception left; the secret tile is a raised tile now.
Don't restyle data: lens pills, map ramps, chart series, game art and the hex terrain keep their own colors.
Don't give an author a palette: guest pieces wear the site's look, and every author is the same card.
Don't ship literal pictogram icons on maps or dashboards; geometric symbols only.
Don't introduce new fonts or new accent hues beyond the six brand colors and brass.
Don't use em dashes anywhere, including UI strings, aria labels, and CSS comments; middots join fragments.
Don't render the 4Ps as page structure or labeled headers; they are pills and picker sections only.
